title: Microwave-driven Synthesis of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles for Fast Detection of Atherosclerosis
protocol: Dissolve 23.8 mg of HEPES in 100 ml of distilled water to prepare 1 mM HEPES Buffer.
Adjust the pH of the HEPES buffer to 7.
Dissolve 10 g of NaHSO3 in 100 ml of distilled water to prepare a 10% NaHSO3 solution.
Stir the NaHSO3 mixture for 15 min.
Dissolve 1 g of NaOH in 100 ml of water to prepare a NaOH solution.
Stir the NaOH solution for 10 min.
Dissolve 600 mg of NaH2PO4 in 1 L of water to prepare a 10 mM Phosphate buffer.
Add carefully 0.34 ml of phosphoric acid to the phosphate buffer and stir for 30 min.
Adjust the pH of the phosphate buffer to 2.9 (acceptance range 2.7-3.0).
Dissolve 269 mg of NaH2PO4 and 1.09 g of Na2HPO4 in distilled water to make a volume of 1 L for another 10 mM Phosphate buffer.
Adjust the pH of this phosphate buffer to 7.2.
Add 0.5 g of Fe(acac)3, 1.4 ml of oleic acid, 0.6 ml of oleylamine, and 1.19 g of 1,2-hexadodecanediol in a microwave adapted flask.
Add 10 ml of phenyl ether carefully through the flask wall using a graduated pipette.
Introduce the flask into the microwave reactor and start the microwave protocol for the synthesis of Oleic Acid Coated Nanoparticles (OA-IONP).
Load a dynamic study in the microwave for Stage 1.
Set the temperature to 60 °C, time to 2 min, pressure to 250 psi, and power to 150 W.
Place stir speed in high position and ensure max power is on.
Proceed to Stage 2 after completing Stage 1.
Set the temperature to 200 °C, time to 20 min, pressure to 250 psi, and power to 300 W for Stage 2.
Ensure stir speed is in high position and max power is on.
Move to Stage 3 upon finishing Stage 2.
Set the temperature to 250 °C, time to 10 min, pressure to 250 psi, and power to 300 W for Stage 3.
Place stir speed in high position and ensure max power is on.
Allow the flask to cool at room temperature after completing all stages.
Wash aggregates from the stir bar and flask wall with EtOH.
Transfer the reaction mixture to an Erlenmeyer using a glass pipette.
Add 10 ml of EtOH 98% to the Erlenmeyer.
Place a Nd-Nb-B magnet below the flask for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant with a glass pipette after magnetic separation.
Repeat washing step three times by adding 10 ml of EtOH, sonicating at room temperature and 40 kHz, then removing the supernatant.
Disperse oleic nanoparticles in 30 ml of CHCl3.
Sonicate the sample for 5 minutes at room temperature and 40 kHz.
Place the sample on a magnet to remove the supernatant after sonication.
Check hydrodynamic size in the zetasizer as per manufacturer's instructions.
Put 0.5 ml of OA-IONP and 0.5 ml of CHCl3 into the glass cuvette for measurement.
Acceptance range is expressed as Z-average size in intensity, with values between 7-10 nm.
Dissolve 44.3 mg of KMnO4 and 150.4 mg of BTACl in a mixture of H2O:CHCl3 (3:2 ml).
Add the resultant solution to a 5 ml aliquot of OA-IONP in the microwave adapted flask.
Set temperature at 105 °C, time at 9 min, pressure at 250 psi and power at 300 W for the microwave protocol.
Put 10 ml of phosphate buffer pH = 2.9 into the flask and repeat the microwave protocol.
Recover nanoparticles using a magnet after cooling and eliminate supernatant.
Add 5 ml of 10% NaHSO3 to an Erlenmeyer flask, sonicate at 40 kHz for 2 min at 25 °C.
Collect particles using a magnet and eliminate supernatant (repeat twice).
Wash nanoparticles three times with 1% NaOH.
Re-disperse nanoparticles in 5 ml of phosphate buffer pH = 7.2.
Put 0.7 ml of Azelaic-IONP into the disposable folded capillary cell for zetasizer analysis.
Add 12 mg of EDC and 15 mg of Sulfo-NHS to an aliquot of Azelaic-IONP in a centrifuge.
Vortex mixture at RT for 35 min.
Put a magnet below the centrifuge to destabilize the nanoparticles.
Aspirate the supernatant and wash the particles with 1.5 ml of HEPES 1 mM pH=7 buffer.
Repeat the washing step two more times.
Add 5 mg of neridronate and shake the mixture in a vortex for 2 hr.
Separate nanoparticles with a magnet and wash three times with 3 x 2 ml of 1 mM HEPES pH=7 buffer.
Disperse Neridronate-IONP in 2 ml of 1mM HEPES pH = 7 buffer.
Check the hydrodynamic size and zeta potential using a disposable folded capillary cell on the zetasizer.
Anesthetize the animals with vaporized isoflurane for induction.
Maintain anesthesia during the MRI experiment with 1-1.5% isoflurane.
Place the animal in the center of the magnet using a profile acquisition.
Tune the RF coil to the 300 MHz resonance frequency at 7 T.
Match the characteristic impedance of the coil to 50 Ohm for optimal signal reception.
Plug the coils into the scanner after tuning and matching.
Calibrate the RF pulse shape and length manually.
Adjust the center frequency manually.
Adjust the receiver gain manually.
Perform a 90° pulse calibration manually.
Conduct coarse shimming manually.
Use a gradient echo (FLASH or GRE) localizer scan for exact position.
Acquire axial, coronal, and sagittal images using a tripilot acquisition.
Optimize magnetic field homogeneity in the center of the magnet through manual magnet shimming.
Inject 100 μl of neridronate nanoparticles intravenously into the tail vein.
Acquire MRI images of the abdominal aorta 1 hour post injection.
Load parameters for MRI acquisition of atherosclerotic plaque, focusing on the renal bifurcation area.
Use multi-slice mode with 10 to 20 slices in interleave mode to minimize artifacts.
Perform high-resolution fast spin echo T1-weighted MRI imaging with FOV settings appropriate for coronal or axial views.
Set slice thickness to 0.8 mm, reducing to 0.6 mm if using a small gradient coil configuration.
Acquire images with TR of 400 msec and TE of 8 msec.
Use a matrix size of 256 x 256 for acquisition and reconstruction.
Average signals 6 (large gradient) to 8 (small gradient) times for image clarity.
Transfer the images using a standard format such as DICOM.
View the transferred images in appropriate software (e.g., Osirix Imaging Software or AMIDE: Medical Imaging Data Examiner).
Quantify the contrast effect manually delimiting the vessel area, wall thickness, lumen area and plaque burden.
